title: Imperfect and present perfect: what has changed

sections.content: You know the imperfect (A2 Unit 21) and the present perfect (A2 Unit 1), and you met their contrast for change over time in B1 Unit 5. Use the imperfect for how things used to be in the colony, and the present perfect for what has changed since then and still matters now.

items.spanish: En 1800 la ley distinguía a las personas por su origen; desde entonces esa regla ha cambiado.
items.english: In 1800 the law distinguished people by origin; since then that rule has changed.

items.spanish: La tierra estaba en pocas manos, y la desigualdad no ha desaparecido.
items.english: Land was in few hands, and inequality has not disappeared.

items.spanish: Antes muchos pueblos indígenas no tenían voz política; en las últimas décadas han ganado más derechos.
items.english: Before, many indigenous peoples had no political voice; in recent decades they have gained more rights.

items.spanish: Los prejuicios eran fuertes en esa época, y todavía no han desaparecido por completo.
items.english: Prejudices were strong at that time, and they have still not completely disappeared.

sections.content: Words like *antes* and *en esa época* point to the imperfect; *desde entonces*, *todavía* and *en las últimas décadas* point to the present perfect, because the result is still true now.
